description: PHASE 5.4 — Multi-Incident Continuous Learning Scenario Dataset

training_incidents.title: Billing Postgres Deadlock and Transaction Rollback Contention
symptoms: deadlock detected in process awaiting ExclusiveLock on relation invoice_ledger
transaction rollback rate exceeding 45% on billing write transactions
p99 billing write latency degraded past 5000ms
training_incidents.root_cause: Concurrent payment finalization workers acquired invoice and customer ledger locks in opposing order under peak invoice billing cycle.
failed_mitigations: Increasing database worker concurrency exacerbated row lock contention and forced db cpu to 99%.
Blindly restarting worker pods left orphaned advisory locks in postgres.
training_incidents.resolution: Applied RB-BILLING-SERIALIZE-TX: enforced deterministic row locking order and added optimistic lock retry backoff.
training_incidents.postmortem_summary: Resolved by executing RB-BILLING-SERIALIZE-TX to sort lock acquisition sequence across invoice and ledger entities.

training_incidents.title: Stripe Gateway Webhook Delivery Timeout & Worker Egress Starvation
symptoms: upstream payment gateway webhook endpoint returned 504 Gateway Timeout
billing_egress_worker_threads pool at 100% capacity
HTTP connection lease timeout connecting to api.stripe.com
training_incidents.root_cause: External payment provider latency spike caused unbounded thread lease waiting on outbound webhook client, starving invoice processing threads.
failed_mitigations: Restarting billing-service pods caused immediate avalanche retry storm of duplicate charge requests to upstream provider.
Increasing egress timeout from 10s to 30s aggravated thread exhaustion.
training_incidents.resolution: Applied RB-GATEWAY-CIRCUIT-TRIP: opened circuit breaker for non-critical webhooks and rerouted pending charges to asynchronous SQS queue.
training_incidents.postmortem_summary: Resolved via RB-GATEWAY-CIRCUIT-TRIP by isolating external stripe webhook egress and buffering outgoing calls.

training_incidents.title: JWT Signing Key Expiration & Redis Keyset Stampede
symptoms: JWT validation cache miss rate spiked from 0.1% to 94%
auth-db queries/sec spiked 20x to 15,000 QPS on public keys table
token verification response time exceeded 3200ms
training_incidents.root_cause: Synchronous expiration of the primary RSA token signing public key invalidated keyset caches across all auth nodes simultaneously, stampeding the auth metadata database.
failed_mitigations: Flushing the auth Redis cluster evicted all active sessions and dropped valid user authentication tokens.
Restarting auth-service pods caused immediate cold-cache thundering herd back onto the auth database.
training_incidents.resolution: Applied RB-AUTH-WARM-KEYSET: pre-warmed Redis cluster with dual active-passive key pairs and configured proactive TTL jitter.
training_incidents.postmortem_summary: Resolved via RB-AUTH-WARM-KEYSET by injecting overlapping active keyset and jittering cache TTLs.

training_incidents.title: Catalog Category Tree Redis TTL Expiry Thundering Herd
symptoms: category_cache_miss_rate exceeded 98% across all catalog replicas
backend catalog search elasticsearch cluster CPU saturated at 96%
p99 category browsing latency spiked to 4800ms
training_incidents.root_cause: Top-level category tree cache key expired with zero jitter during flash sales, triggering distributed thundering herd queries to the Elasticsearch backend.
failed_mitigations: Disabling Redis caching and querying Elasticsearch directly tripped backend cluster overload circuit breakers.
Increasing JVM heap on catalog-service pods caused severe Stop-the-World garbage collection pauses.
training_incidents.resolution: Applied RB-CATALOG-STAGGER-TTL: populated category hierarchy with probabilistic early expiration (XFetch algorithm) and warm cache priming.
training_incidents.postmortem_summary: Resolved via RB-CATALOG-STAGGER-TTL: mitigated cache stampede by staggering key expiry and warming category index.

training_incidents.title: Kafka Consumer Heartbeat Starvation and Cascading Rebalance Storm
symptoms: CommitFailedException: max.poll.interval.ms exceeded on event-pipeline-consumer
consumer group rebalance storm: group state stuck in PreparingRebalance
kafka consumer group message lag exceeded 250,000 records
training_incidents.root_cause: Excessive JSON batch payload sizes caused consumer processing loop to exceed max.poll.interval.ms, triggering repeated coordinator partition revoking and rebalancing.
failed_mitigations: Forcefully restarting out-of-sync consumer pods caused cascading partition reassignment across the entire consumer cluster.
Reducing session.timeout.ms caused false positive node dead detections and escalated rebalance frequency.
training_incidents.resolution: Applied RB-KAFKA-EXTEND-MAX-POLL: dynamically doubled max.poll.interval.ms to 600,000ms, reduced max.poll.records to 100, and stabilized consumer heartbeat thread.
training_incidents.postmortem_summary: Resolved via RB-KAFKA-EXTEND-MAX-POLL by decoupling heartbeats and tuning poll intervals.

training_incidents.title: Draft Postmortem: Elasticsearch Field Data Cache Overflow & JVM Pressure
symptoms: circuit_breaking_exception: [parent] Data too large, data for fielddata would be larger than limit
fielddata cache consumption exceeded 60% of JVM heap
training_incidents.root_cause: Unverified draft postmortem hypothesis: unindexed text field aggregation caused unbounded heap consumption.
failed_mitigations: Unverified AI draft action: restart cluster nodes one by one without disabling shard allocation.
